one_liner: Fails the quality test (no free cash flow), so price does not matter.

profile.what: Amazon is the largest online retailer in the US and runs Amazon Web Services (AWS), the largest cloud-computing provider. It also sells advertising, Prime memberships and streaming video.
profile.money: Online retail is most of revenue but earns thin margins. AWS earns most of the operating profit, charging companies for computing and storage. Advertising on its shopping sites, fees from third-party sellers who use its warehouses, and Prime subscriptions are increasingly important profit sources.
profile.valued: Amazon is valued on EV/EBITDA, operating cash flow and a sum of the parts, because heavy investment keeps reported earnings and free cash flow low. The multiple moves with AWS growth and the return on its AI capital spending.

summary.sentence: The leader in online retail and cloud computing, reinvesting nearly all its cash in AI capacity.
strengths: AWS and advertising are high-margin and growing.
Today's capex builds capacity for years of AI demand.
risks: TTM free cash flow is about -$47B: there is no cash to value yet.
TTM net income includes large non-operating gains.

meaning.what_it_does: Runs the largest online store in the West, AWS cloud computing, a fast-growing ad business, Prime and logistics.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Retail sales and third-party seller fees, AWS cloud services (most of operating profit), advertising and subscriptions.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Prime loyalty, unmatched logistics and AWS's head start keep customers; advertising rides on top of the shopping traffic.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: If the AI data-centre build-out fails to earn its cost, free cash flow stays negative; or retail margins get squeezed by competition and regulation.

moat.summary: Fast, cheap delivery at Amazon's scale is extremely hard to copy, and moving off AWS is costly for enterprises.

industry.summary: Retail moves slowly; cloud and AI infrastructure move fast and need constant investment.

management.summary: Long-term owner mindset and strong execution, but a pattern of spending every dollar of operating cash on growth leaves little for owners today.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $47.7B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 2.7x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 11–17% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 13%; cost of capital 9.2%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
